current_state: Six-theme evidence brief and Google Drive source-asset audit v1 are committed to main. No source image or derived cutout was pushed to the public repository.
strongest_findings: 2026 fashion visibility supports beads and semiprecious stones as a current jewelry language, but does not prove theme-level demand or justify copying maximalist multicolor runway styling.
User Drive references are most useful for structural cues: asymmetric focal placement, material zoning, low-metal dark neutral language, and transparency/size rhythm.
The current 22 Drive images are third-party social screenshots, not production-grade clean single-bead sources; forcing cutouts would reduce material fidelity and add rights risk.
Forest/Mountain can directly benefit from REF-G02, Starlight from REF-G06, Glacier from REF-G03; Ocean should use REF-G05 as a deep-water contrast reference rather than a literal copy.
evidence_limits: No verified Europe-wide sales, conversion or theme-level revenue dataset was obtained.
Editorial visibility evidence is not demand evidence.
Etsy listing/cart/seller signals are low-strength demand proxies only.
Drive upload does not equal explicit preference, and images cannot confirm mineral identity, treatment, origin or grade.
risks_blockers: Clean rights-cleared single-bead/loose-stone source photos are still missing for Workbench real sprites.
The 18-design package had not yet appeared when this task was executed, so material-source priority could not be narrowed by actual BOM frequency.
Public repository status prohibits pushing private/third-party Drive source images or derived cutouts without explicit publication rights.
next_action: Design Agent should consume theme-evidence-brief-v1 immediately for the 18-design package. After the design JSON appears, re-rank real-image sourcing by BOM frequency and request/source clean rights-cleared photos only for high-frequency launch materials.
